record.context_brief: universal ordering for bounded Gabor representations
record.original_question: Is there a single universal ordering rule {f_k}_{k in I} that works for every overcomplete Gabor frame that admits some bounded-operator orbit representation, so that whenever a frame {E_{mb}T_{na}g}_{m,n in Z} is of a type covered by the previous existence question, arranging its elements according to that one rule always yields {f_k}_{k in I}={T^k phi}_{k in I} for a bounded operator T?

evidence.quote: (P1-d) Is there a universal ordering on the form {fk}k∈I that applies for all the Gabor frames in (P1-c)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. For $a,b>0$ and $g\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$, the associated Gabor system is
$$\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}},\qquad (T_x f)(t)=f(t-x),\ (E_y f)(t)=e^{2\pi i y t}f(t).$$
Such a system is called a Gabor frame if there exist constants $0<A\le B<\infty$ with
$$A\|f\|^2\le\sum_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}|\langle f,E_{mb}T_{na}g\rangle|^2\le B\|f\|^2\qquad(f\in L^2(\mathbb{R})),$$
and is overcomplete if it remains a frame after removing any one element.

Given a sequence $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ indexed by an ordered set $I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, we say it is represented as an orbit of a bounded operator if there exist $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and a bounded linear operator $T:L^2(\mathbb{R})\to L^2(\mathbb{R})$ such that $f_k=T^k\varphi$ for all $k\in I$.

Let $\mathcal{G}$ denote the class of overcomplete Gabor frames $\{E_{mb}T_{na}g\}_{m,n\in\mathbb{Z}}$ that, after some bijective relabelling by an index set $I\subseteq\mathbb{Z}$, can be written as the orbit $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}$ of a bounded operator $T$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$.

Question. Does there exist a single universal ordering rule — that is, a fixed scheme assigning to each Gabor frame in $\mathcal{G}$ a bijective enumeration $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ of its elements (depending only on the parameters $a,b$ and the window $g$ via this fixed rule) — such that for every frame in $\mathcal{G}$ the resulting enumeration $\{f_k\}_{k\in I}$ has the form $\{T^k\varphi\}_{k\in I}$ for some bounded operator $T$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ and some $\varphi\in L^2(\mathbb{R})$?
artifact.category_tag: Gabor frames and operator orbit representations
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Christensen, Hasannasab, and collaborators (e.g., "Orbits of bounded bijective operators and Gabor frames", 2020; "Frame properties of operator orbits", 2020; and later surveys) establishes strong constraints — for instance, overcomplete Gabor frames cannot be written as orbits $(T^n f_0)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ of a bounded operator, and certain classes cannot even be ordered over $\mathbb{Z}$ as orbits of invertible bounded operators. However, no located source explicitly resolves the universal-ordering question for the class of overcomplete Gabor frames that do admit bounded-operator orbit representations; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Orbits of bounded bijective operators and Gabor frames
status_evidence.snippet: Two classes of overcomplete Gabor frames which cannot be ordered over Z and represented by orbits of operators in GL(L^2(R)) are given.
status_evidence.claim: Provides negative results on Z-ordering of overcomplete Gabor frames as bounded-operator orbits, but does not resolve the universal-ordering question.

status_evidence.title: A Survey on Frame Representations and Operator Orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of operator-orbit representations of frames including open questions on Gabor frame orbit representations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent survey indicates the universal-ordering problem for Gabor frames admitting bounded-operator orbit representations remains among the open questions.

status_evidence.title: Frame properties of operator orbits
status_evidence.snippet: Frame-theoretic properties of orbits of bounded operators are developed.
status_evidence.claim: Develops the framework but does not provide a universal ordering rule for the relevant class of Gabor frames.
